entries.name: Sea Cliff Bridge

facts.claim: The Sea Cliff Bridge is 665 m long and is a highlight of the Grand Pacific Drive; it opened in December 2005, lets visitors get out of the car and stretch their legs, and is a viewing platform for migrating whales.
Pedestrians can walk along the bridge; the flat rocky area below has marine life at low tide.
The bridge carries two traffic lanes and a pedestrian walkway on Lawrence Hargrave Drive between Coalcliff and Clifton.

entries.name: Nan Tien Temple

facts.claim: Nan Tien Temple, opened in October 1995, is a branch temple of Fo Guang Shan and the biggest Buddhist temple in Australia; it contains a vegetarian restaurant and has won awards for its lighting, gardens and architecture.
Open Tuesday to Sunday and public holidays 9am-5pm, closed Mondays except public holidays; gates should be reached by 4:30pm.
Entry and parking are free (180 Berkeley Road, Berkeley).

entries.name: Mount Keira Lookout

facts.claim: Mount Keira is 463.9 m high, 4 km north-west of Wollongong's CBD, and gives sweeping views over the city; Mount Keira Lookout is on Mt Keira Road and is accessible seven days a week during daylight hours.
There is a cafe at the top serving Devonshire teas, hang-gliders launch nearby, and the lookout is free; the 5 km Mount Keira Ring Track circles the mountain.
The 5.5 km Mt Keira Ring Track starts and finishes at a scenic picnic spot.

entries.name: Wollongong Head Lighthouse

facts.claim: Wollongong Head Lighthouse (Flagstaff Point Light) is an active lighthouse beside the heritage-listed Wollongong Harbour precinct, on Flagstaff Point east of the city centre.
The larger Flagstaff Hill lighthouse is active and sits right next to the inactive 12 m Breakwater Lighthouse; Wollongong is the only point on Australia's east coast with two lighthouses.
The lighthouse is on Endeavour Drive.

entries.name: Sublime Point Lookout

facts.claim: Sublime Point Lookout offers 180-degree views over the sea, the rainforest and the 17 beaches that span the coastline to Wollongong; barbecues, picnic shelters and toilets are provided (bring your own drinking water).
Sublime Point is probably the most famous of the three Bulli Pass lookouts, best for a picnic or the view; it can be reached by car or a steep hike, and is free.
The Sublime Point walking track starts near the viewing platform.

entries.name: Wollongong Botanic Garden

facts.claim: The garden covers 27 hectares of gardens, winding pathways and plant collections, with views over Wollongong from Gleniffer Brae Manor House; it is open daily.
Hours listed: Monday to Friday 7:00am-6:00pm, Saturday 7:00am-6:45pm.
The garden is across from the University of Wollongong, with duck ponds and short walks, and is free.

entries.name: Stanwell Park

facts.claim: Stanwell Park is famous for paragliding and hang gliding from Bald Hill down to its beach, which lies nested between high sea cliffs.
Stanwell Park is a small quaint coastal town on the northern edge of the Illawarra; the Grand Pacific Drive passes through it on its way to the Sea Cliff Bridge.
Stanwell Park has a train station with hourly services and is one of the best stations for nearby beaches.

entries.name: North Beach Wollongong

facts.claim: North Wollongong Beach has rock pools, wading areas and good surf, with grass, shade, picnic booths, a playground nearby in Stuart Park, shops and cafes; parking is free.
It is the only beach patrolled all year round.
North Beach is one of Wollongong's most popular beaches, in front of Stuart Park and the Novotel, with a kiosk on the beach.

entries.name: Austinmer Beach

facts.claim: Austinmer Beach is one of Wollongong's most popular beaches, about 20 minutes north of the CBD, patrolled September to April, with shops along the western side and a large car park and park between the beach and the road.
Austinmer is a very pleasant cove and small beach with cafes and restaurants across the road and barbecues behind; it can suffer from popularity, so go early or late on a sunny day.
Austinmer train station is among the best for accessing nearby beaches.

entries.name: Kiama Blowhole

facts.claim: The 2.5 m opening in the rock has thrown plumes recorded above 30 m, best when the swell runs from the south-east; there are several accessible viewing platforms, and the most eastern point shows the full height of the rock formation.
It is estimated to attract 900,000 visitors a year.
Kiama Blowhole and Lighthouse are on Blowhole Point Rd; free to visit. The Little Blowhole, further south, is best in north-easterly winds.

entries.name: Kiama Coast Walk

facts.claim: The Kiama Coast Walk is about 20 km from the mouth of the Minnamurra River south through Kiama to Gerringong's Werri Beach, in three sections of sealed paths, grassed tracks and beach walking.

North section: Minnamurra River to Kiama Blowhole, 8.5 km, about 3 hrs. Mid section: Blowhole to Loves Bay, 6 km, about 1.5 hrs (the Little Blowhole is midway). South section: Loves Bay to Gerringong, 6 km, about 2 hrs.
The walk can be tackled in sections and runs roughly parallel to the train line.

entries.name: Jamberoo Action Park

facts.claim: 2026-27 season adult (13-59 years) ticket: $84 online, $94 at the gate; ages 4-12 and 60+ $74 online, $84 gate; children 3 and under free. It is cheapest to buy online direct from the park.
Open 10am-5pm on open days; the park is open Friday to Sunday through October, with a Six Weeks of Summer program (daily dates are on the Open Hours page); 1215 Jamberoo Road.
Rides include Velocity Falls, The Stinger, The Perfect Storm, Funnel Web, The Taipan, Bobsled, Rapid River and a chairlift.

entries.name: Gerringong

facts.claim: Gerringong is the first coastal town south of Kiama and considerably quieter than its northern neighbour; it surrounds the beach suburb of Werri Beach.
Gerringong Whale Watching Platform on Tasman Drive is a small viewing deck for spotting whales between May and November.
The town has two beaches, Gerringong Beach and Werri Beach, great for swimming in peace; the Kiama Coast Walk ends at Werri Beach.

Shellharbour Visitor Information Centre is on Addison St, Shellharbour Village (listed 9AM-5PM, updated 2017).
Killalea State Park, Mystics Beach and Bass Point skydives are nearby; Shell Cove is a major housing development beside the town.

The lookout is 10 minutes from Kiama's Blowhole.
Saddleback Mountain Lookout is 7 km south-west of Kiama, reached from Saddleback Mountain Road, up a winding scenic drive through dairy country.

entries.name: Minnamurra Beach

facts.claim: Minnamurra Beach is the surf break of Killalea Regional Park, 'also known as Mystics to the locals'.

At the outlet of the Minnamurra River the beach ends in a long sand spit jutting towards Stack Island, popular for kayaking and stand-up paddling; the ocean side has strong waves and can be dangerous, the river side is shallow with tidal currents.
Mystics Beach: 1.5 km of beach; access is via a steep path down from the car park; no lifeguards or other facilities.

entries.name: HARS Australian Historical Flying Museum

facts.claim: HARS Aviation Museum at Shellharbour Airport (54 Airport Road, Albion Park Rail) is open Monday to Sunday 9:30am-3:30pm (last tour at 2pm), except Christmas Day and Airshow Days; entry is by guided tour of working hangars.
Museum entrance fees from 1 July 2025: adult (15+) $35, concession $30, child (5-14) $15, family (2 adults and up to 4 children) $80.
The museum has about 50 aircraft at Shellharbour, nearly 20 airworthy; the Boeing 747-438 VH-OJA is on display and can be walked on in the Wing Walk tour.

Remnant rainforest with Moreton Bay figs, headland views, and birdlife including Australian bitterns and pied oystercatchers.

facts.claim: Minnamurra Rainforest Centre in Budderoo National Park: wander elevated walkways through rare remnant rainforest; the Lyrebird loop walk takes an hour; residents include superb lyrebird, eastern water dragon and swamp wallaby.
Centre open 9am to 4pm daily, closed Christmas Day; park gates at Minnamurra Rainforest Centre open 9am and close 5pm every day.
Park entry fee: $12 per vehicle per day, only in the Minnamurra Rainforest area; bus or taxi $4.40 per adult and $2.20 per child.

entries.name: Carrington Falls

facts.claim: Carrington Falls, where the Kangaroo River plunges over 50 m, has cascades, waterholes and rockpools that some regard as the most beautiful on the South Coast; there are three lookouts, picnic and barbecue facilities and short walking tracks.
Park entry fees apply in the Minnamurra Rainforest area only, so there is no entry fee at Carrington Falls picnic area.
Izzards lookout track is a short walk; the Warris Chair and Missingham lookout tracks are longer, from Nellies Glen picnic area.

entries.name: Macquarie Pass National Park

facts.claim: Macquarie Pass National Park on the Illawarra escarpment is an easy day trip from the southern suburbs of Sydney, with rainforest, bushwalking, birdwatching, waterfalls, ocean views and Illawarra flame trees in flower.
Cascades walk: 2 km return, 45 min to 1 hr 15 min, Grade 3, an easy walk through shady rainforest to a waterfall and pool near Kiama and Robertson.
Cascades picnic area is a sunny picnic area amid the rainforest, a break from the road trip or a rest after Cascades walk.

entries.name: Fitzroy Falls

facts.claim: Fitzroy Falls lookout is 150 m from the Fitzroy Falls Visitor Centre: a wheelchair-accessible elevated boardwalk to the escarpment edge, from where the falls drop nearly 100 m (the visitor centre page says over 80 m) into the Yarrunga Valley.
Fitzroy Falls Visitor Centre, 1301 Nowra Road, is open 9am to 4pm daily and closed Christmas Day; West Rim walking track and East Rim Wildflower walking track start nearby.
Park entry fee at Fitzroy Falls: $4 per vehicle per day (Bundanoon area $8); pay machines take cash and cards.

entries.name: Belmore Falls

facts.claim: Belmore Falls walking track is a short walk to several lookouts with views over Kangaroo Valley: 1.8 km return, 30 min to 1 hr, Grade 3.
All access to the base of Belmore Falls is permanently closed.
Park entry fees apply at Fitzroy Falls and in the Bundanoon area of Morton National Park, not at Belmore Falls; reaching the falls from Robertson involves a narrow winding dirt road.

entries.name: Kangaroo Valley

facts.claim: Kangaroo Valley is a fully enclosed valley with a small town (population 900) offering a historic suspension bridge, buildings and antique stores to browse; it is the historic home of the Wodi-Wodi people.
The village is tiny and all buildings are a few minutes' walk apart; Hampden Bridge is over a kilometre away.
A scenic route runs along Upper Kangaroo River Road to a flat rock picnic spot; the last kilometres are unsealed.

entries.name: Hampden Bridge

facts.claim: Hampden Bridge, a heritage-listed single-span suspension bridge over the Kangaroo River, opened on 19 May 1898, six days before floods washed away the old timber bridge; designed by Ernest de Burgh, built by Loveridge and Hudson.
It is the second suspension bridge built in NSW and the only surviving suspension road bridge from the 19th century.
The stone pillars tower over the river below; the bridge dates from 1889 per the Wikivoyage listing (Wikipedia and the NSW heritage listing say 1898).

entries.name: Fleet Air Arm Museum

facts.claim: The museum tells the story of Australian naval aviation in a hangar-style main exhibition hall and two art galleries at the entrance of HMAS Albatross, overlooking the runway, with aircraft, technology, models, clothing and memorabilia.
Open 10am to 4pm Friday to Sunday and public holidays; Tuesday to Sunday during school holidays; closed Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day.
Admission is free per the Navy's museum page (as reported in a search summary; the Navy page itself could not be loaded by script).

entries.name: Berry

facts.claim: Berry is an elegant village with a charming main street in the Shoalhaven; learn the town's history at the Berry Historic Museum or along the self-guided Berry Historical Walk, and browse antiques in heritage buildings.
The Berry Donut Van on Queen Street is a local institution for cinnamon doughnuts.
Berry is easily walkable if you are just browsing antique and craft shops; Berry Museum (135 Queen St) opens Saturday 11am-2pm and Sunday 11am-3pm (2021 listing).

entries.name: Seven Mile Beach National Park

facts.claim: Seven Mile Beach National Park lies between Shoalhaven Heads and Gerroa and offers fishing, swimming, picnicking and walking; Beach Road picnic area has everything for a relaxing day at the beach and a lookout over the beach.
Sand track walk (north): 3 km one-way, 2 hr 30 min to 3 hr 30 min, through forest and back along the beach.
The park is always open but may close in poor weather or fire danger.

entries.name: Wollongong

facts.claim: Wollongong stretches over 40 km south to north along a coastal strip between the escarpment and the sea, never more than about 6 km wide, from Port Kembla to Stanwell Park.
Highlights include Sublime Point and Mount Keira lookouts, Nan Tien Temple, the harbour lighthouses, the Botanic Garden and beaches such as North Beach and Austinmer.
The Grand Pacific Drive and the Sea Cliff Bridge link Wollongong with Sydney's Royal National Park.

entries.name: Kiama

facts.claim: Kiama is about 90 minutes south of Sydney by car and just over 2 hours by train, famous for its spectacular coastline and rural scenery.
It is an easy walk from the train station to the beach, the blowhole and the shopping centre.
Central Kiama has a harbour rather than a beach, with patrolled beaches to the north and south and a tidal rockpool beside the blowhole.

entries.name: Nowra

facts.claim: Nowra is a town of 29,000 on the Shoalhaven River, 163 km south of Sydney, the chief administrative and business centre of Shoalhaven City and a regional centre for tourism.
Bomaderry, its twin town north of the river, has the train station; a bus connects over the road bridge to Nowra.
Nowra is an Aboriginal word meaning 'black cockatoo'; the traditional owners south of the river are the Wandi-Wandandian of the Yuin nation.
